 CHENEY, Wash. — After a brutal 62-31 loss to rival Idaho, Eastern Washington is looking to put another disappointing performance behind it as the Eagles prepare for their final two games of the season.
 On this week's episode of Talking Eags , AJ Howell and the voice of the Eagles, Larry Weir, broke down Eastern's struggles against Idaho, the challenges facing the program and what to expect when EWU travels to Utah Tech on Saturday.
 "It was a butt-kicking from the kickoff, basically," Weir said. "Idaho scored touchdowns on all five possessions in the first half. They scored on their first nine possessions of the game, not all touchdowns, but they scored on their first nine."
 The Vandals dominated the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball, rushing for 335 yards while holding Eastern to just 50 yards on the ground.
 Idaho jumped out to a 35-10 halftime lead and never looked back.
 "I don't think there was anything they could take away from that game that was a positive," Weir said. "It was more than one step back, I would say, even from the Montana State game, which was a rout as well."
 The loss continued what has been a difficult season for Eastern, which is now facing the possibility of finishing with one of its worst records since moving to Division I.
 However, Weir believes comparing the current program to past Eastern teams is difficult, especially with how much college football has changed through NIL and the transfer portal.
 "The way Eastern always did things is they would recruit high school players, redshirt them their first year, develop them, and by the time they were juniors and seniors, some cases it happened earlier, you'd have valuable contributors to your team," Weir said.
 "That's all, the way they built the program is all out the window now because NIL and free transfers."
 Despite the struggles, Weir pointed out that Eastern has been competitive at times against some of the top teams in the FCS, including Northern Arizona, Montana and South Dakota, but has struggled to put together complete performances.
 Now, with just two games remaining, the Eagles have an opportunity to finish the season on a positive note.
 Eastern travels to St. George, Utah, on Saturday, Nov. 14, for its first-ever meeting with Utah Tech before returning home to close the season against Portland State.
 Utah Tech has struggled with turnovers in recent weeks, including three against UC Davis, while its defense has allowed nearly 40 points per game.
 Weir believes Eastern's offense should have opportunities to put points on the board, but the biggest question remains whether the Eagles can limit explosive plays defensively.
 "Utah Tech averages 19 points a game. So if they can keep them in the 20s and the low-to-mid 20s, especially, I think they will have a really good chance of winning this game," Weir said.
 "If Eastern plays well defensively, they've got a really good chance to win this game."
 EWU and Utah Tech kick off at 1 p.m. Saturday.
